correctness.rationale: PASS: For d>=2, M=2^(d-1), budget sum_j S_j+tT=B, singleton Walsh characters have Rayleigh quotients 2(S_j+T)/M; two-coordinate Walsh characters have 2(S_i+S_j)/M. Family averages give global bounds A(T)=2[B+(d-t)T]/(Md) and C(T)=4(B-tT)/(Md) for every asymmetric assignment. Crossing at T=B/(d+t) if t<d and A monotonic for t>d gives the piecewise optimum; constant class weights attain it by full Walsh spectrum 2a|J|+2b 1_{|J|odd}. At optimum, equal averages imply each relevant Walsh character is an actual lambda2-eigenvector, so pointwise equations force w_j(x)=v(x)=lambda2/4 for t<d; t>d forces T=0 and w_j(x)=lambda2/2. At t=d singleton-eigenvector conditions force w_j(x)+v(x)=constant, edge symmetry and connectedness force v(x), hence all ordinary edges, constant; the critical optimum face is a+b=B/(Md), 0<=b<=a. The d=2 separate algebra is sound. Independent weighted Laplacian eigenvalue calculations for d=2,3,4, B=7, t=0.5,d,d+1 reproduce predicted lambda2; finite examples only corroborate the global Rayleigh proof.

evidence: Sun et al provide the convex/spectral framework with graph-independent duality; Boyd et al use symmetry reduction for discrete chains and ordinary hypercube characters.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Framework existence/convexity does not imply the exact t=d kink or that every optimum is class-uniform. Equality eigenvector equations are the indispensable new argument. Symmetry averaging produces one symmetric optimizer, never by itself proves absence of asymmetric optima.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge: the continuous-time fastest-mixing optimization/Semidefinite framework, Walsh spectrum of hypercubes, and unweighted folded-hypercube eigenvalues predate this work. The contribution is the price threshold at t=d and equality-case characterization ruling out *all* asymmetric optimizers under freely assigned weights, not symmetry reduction alone.
